subject: Balancing forensic log utility with selective PII masking for ClearTrace Health
messages:
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@cleartracehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: can Redwood provide PII-masked logs but keep forensic value?

Hi Markus & Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — we’re completing a SIG/CAIQ and ClearTrace needs to reconcile two requirements: 1) we must not receive raw patient-identifiable fields in logs (PHI/PII), and 2) our security team needs high-fidelity logs to support incident investigations and billing reconciliation for at least 90 days.

We attached a small sample log (log-sample-20280630.txt) and our draft SIG question set. Our asks: can Redwood produce log exports with selected fields redacted or pseudonymized while preserving time-order, request IDs, session linkage and the ability to correlate events for a forensics timeline? If so, what approach do you recommend (hashing, tokenization, truncation) and how would you document the process for auditors (SOC 2 evidence)?

If there are any contract-level implications (exceptions or limited-scope retention), please outline what you need from us. We may also need a short, signed statement for our vendor risk team describing the controls/configuration.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah Jensen
Head of InfoSec, ClearTrace Health

Attachments: log-sample-20280630.txt; SIG-questions-draft.xlsx
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@cleartracehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: can Redwood provide PII-masked logs but keep forensic value?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear write-up and the sample. Short answer: yes, we can support a selective-masking workflow that preserves the forensic signals you described, but we need to align on the exact fields and the retention/exception window.

Options I’d propose for ClearTrace:
- Pseudonymization using salted HMACs for identified fields (email, user_id, device id). This preserves linkage without exposing raw values.
- Tokenization with reversible tokens stored in a customer-scoped, encrypted vault (helpful if you require re-identification for legal holds).
- Deterministic truncation for low-risk fields (first 3 characters of an ID).

Tradeoffs: reversible tokenization lets you rehydrate for an audit/legal hold but increases the scope of sensitive storage. HMACs preserve forensic correlation with lower risk but cannot re-identify without the original value.

What we need from you to proceed:
1) A list of fields you require redacted vs those that may remain (e.g., timestamps, request_id should remain).
2) Confirmation on the temporary exception for retaining unredacted material (if any) and the requested window.
3) Whether ClearTrace requires a signed attestation (we can provide one for SOC 2 evidence).

I’ve looped in Neha for the security/implementation details and Aditya for commercial/contract implications. We can prepare a short exception proposal + MAP and a technical appendix for your SIG.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@cleartracehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: can Redwood provide PII-masked logs but keep forensic value? (implementation note)

Hi all — technical notes from security/ops side on how we’d implement and evidence this for SIG/SOC2: 

Proposal:
1) For production log streams we will emit two views: a) operational view (masked before export) and b) internal forensic view (full) retained only in an isolated, customer-scoped S3 bucket with strict ACLs, KMS-encryption and FIPS-compliant keys.
2) Masking approach: HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer salt for email/user_ids + canonicalization. Keep timestamps, request_id, session_id intact.
3) Access controls: forensic bucket access is limited to Redwood Security Ops with just-in-time access (JIT) and MFA + short-lived credentials. All access is logged to immutable audit trails.
4) Retention/exception: default masked exports provided; unmasked forensic copies kept for 90 days if customer requests an exception; we will support legal-hold overrides with documented chain-of-custody. After 90 days the forensic copy will be shredded (crypto-delete) and masking becomes the only stored form.
5) Evidence: we can provide an appendix containing configuration snapshots, KMS key aliases, access logs (redacted), and a representative hashing script as evidence for your auditor.

Caveats: reversible tokenization is possible but increases our scope (KMS access/rotations, additional audit responsibilities). If ClearTrace wants re-identification capability for disputes we ask that tokenization be restricted to a sub-scope and paired with an admin-only approval workflow.

I’ll prepare a short technical appendix and a sample SIG answer that explains controls and proof points.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG-answers-partial-redact-20280701.pdf
From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@cleartracehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Morgan Forensics <forensics@morgan-co.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: can Redwood provide PII-masked logs but keep forensic value?

Thanks Neha — this is exactly the kind of detail our vendor team needs. A few clarifying points from our side before we finalize: 
1) For the 90-day unmasked exception: ClearTrace needs an auditable process to request, approve and document the exception. The request will typically come from our legal team and may cite an active subpoena or litigated billing dispute.
2) We need a written SLA on evidence delivery timing (e.g., 48–72 hours to provide exported forensic logs once a valid request/hold is raised).
3) For the permanent deletion step: can you confirm the mechanism (crypto-delete vs object lifecycle) and whether Redwood provides a deletion certificate?

If we can get a short statement describing the exception workflow + SLAs and a draft attestation for the SIG, we can proceed to sign the vendor form. Also please confirm that the forensic bucket will be excluded from downstream analytics that ClearTrace-managed tooling might have access to.

If helpful we can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow morning to walk through the MAP and the proposed attestation language.

Regards,
Sarah

Date: 2028-07-03T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: can Redwood provide PII-masked logs but keep forensic value? — proposed exception process and next steps

Sarah — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. We’re aligned and can commit to the following controlled exception + MAP: 

1) Exception scope: ClearTrace may request a temporary unmasked forensic copy of customer logs for specific legal/forensic reasons. Requests must be initiated by an authorized contact from ClearTrace Legal or InfoSec via an authenticated support/portal flow and include a justification and timeframe.

2) Retention window: unmasked forensic copy retained in an isolated, customer-scoped bucket for up to 90 days by default. If a documented legal hold is provided within that window, we will extend retention and document the chain-of-custody.

3) Access & approval: Access requires Redwood Security Ops approval, JIT MFA, and multi-operator sign-off. All access is logged and included in the evidence packet.

4) Evidence SLA: 72 hours to provide an exported forensic bundle after a validated request (we will target 48 hours for critical legal holds; times subject to scope).

5) Deletion mechanism: after window expiry we perform crypto-delete (KMS key rotation + object lifecycle enforcement) and provide a deletion certificate (signed statement referencing object prefixes, KMS key alias and timestamp).

6) Documentation: I will attach a short exception-process doc and a draft attestation you can include in the SIG. We’ll also produce a compact technical appendix (hashing approach, key id, sample access logs) for SOC 2 evidence.

Next steps:
- I’ll upload the exception-process-doc-20280703.pdf and the draft attestation to the shared link and create a MAP in HubSpot (HT-48321).
- Aditya will follow up on contract/AMEND language for the one-time exception and any billing/commit impacts.
- Neha will produce the SIG-friendly appendix and an operator-runbook for access requests.

If that sounds good I’ll prepare the DocuSign amendment and the short attestation for your vendor team. Happy to take a quick call tomorrow AM to finalize.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
